stem: Sketch the graph of $y = {=a}\cos\theta {=signed(q)}$ for $\theta \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ without using a table of values. How many $x$-intercepts does your sketch have?
solution: The amplitude is $|a| = {=abs(a)}$ and the vertical shift is $q = {=q}$, so the midline is the line $y = {=q}$.
The graph therefore lies between its least value ${=q - abs(a)}$ and its greatest value ${=q + abs(a)}$.

The $x$-axis is the line $y = 0$. The graph cuts it only if $0$ lies strictly between the least and the greatest value, which happens exactly when $|q| < |a|$, that is when the shift is smaller than the amplitude. Then the graph crosses the axis once on the way down and once on the way up. If $|q| > |a|$ the whole graph stays on one side of the axis and never reaches it.
notes: Advanced: combines the effect of a (amplitude) with the effect of q (shift) to decide whether the sketch reaches the x-axis. The case |q| = |a| (graph only touches the axis, at 0 and 360 degrees or at 180 degrees) is excluded so the answer is unambiguous; q = 0 is excluded so the shift always prints. Answer is 2 when |q| < |a| and 0 when |q| > |a|; both occur equally often over the parameter space (40 each; verified by counting sign changes of the sampled curve). Intercepts are interior points of the interval, so the count does not depend on how the end points are treated.
